content.value_statement: Hybrid environments are hard to design because workloads, networks, compliance, and costs span many platforms. This skill guides architecture decisions across public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes, edge, and operations.
actual_capabilities: Compares AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, VMware, and Kubernetes placement options.
Plans hybrid connectivity using dedicated links, VPNs, DNS, routing, and load balancing.
Maps workloads to compliance, latency, data gravity, cost, and performance requirements.
Outlines IaC, GitOps, monitoring, backup, and disaster recovery practices.
Supports FinOps, migration, modernization, and edge architecture planning.
limitations: Does not deploy infrastructure or run cloud provider commands by itself.
Requires current pricing, quotas, and service availability from the user environment.
Cannot validate compliance without organization policies and evidence.
May need provider documentation for newly released services.

use_cases.title: Plan a regulated hybrid architecture
use_cases.description: Design workload placement, network segmentation, identity, encryption, and recovery for regulated systems.

use_cases.title: Modernize on-premises platforms
use_cases.description: Create a migration path from VMware, OpenStack, or legacy systems into a hybrid cloud model.

use_cases.title: Control multi-cloud cost and operations
use_cases.description: Build FinOps, monitoring, automation, and governance practices across several cloud providers.

prompt_templates.title: Assess hybrid cloud goals
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery for a new architecture effort.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me assess whether hybrid cloud is appropriate. Ask for the business goals, workloads, compliance needs, current platforms, budget limits, and timeline.

prompt_templates.title: Compare workload placement options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare placement options for these workloads across AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, VMware, and Kubernetes. Consider cost, latency, compliance, data gravity, and operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design secure hybrid connectivity
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hybrid connectivity approach for my environment. Include dedicated links, VPN fallback, DNS, routing, segmentation, identity integration, monitoring, and failure scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Create a full migration and operations plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased hybrid cloud migration and operating model. Include workload sequencing, automation, observability, FinOps, disaster recovery, compliance controls, risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A bank needs to keep customer data on premises while using cloud analytics for derived datasets.
output: Recommended private placement for regulated source systems with controlled cloud analytics zones.
Identity federation, encryption, audit logging, and data classification controls for each boundary.
A phased validation plan covering latency, compliance evidence, backup, and recovery testing.

output_examples.input: A manufacturer wants edge processing at plants with central management across two public clouds.
output: Edge placement guidance for low-latency workloads and local data preprocessing.
Central governance model for Kubernetes, image distribution, monitoring, and policy enforcement.
Connectivity and failover recommendations for plant outages and cloud service disruption.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants to reduce hybrid cloud spend without breaking performance targets.
output: A cost model that separates compute, storage, network transfer, support, and operational effort.
Right-sizing, reserved capacity, placement, and decommissioning opportunities.
Metrics for budget alerts, chargeback, utilization, and service-level validation.

best_practices: Start with workload requirements before choosing providers or platforms.
Document network, identity, compliance, recovery, and cost assumptions.
Validate designs with current provider limits, pricing, and organizational policies.
anti_patterns: Choosing multiple clouds without a clear workload or resilience reason.
Treating network, identity, and security controls as afterthoughts.
Assuming disaster recovery works without testing failover and restore paths.

faq.question: Does this skill support AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers AWS, Azure, GCP, private cloud, Kubernetes, and edge architecture planning.

faq.question: Can it design OpenStack or VMware hybrid environments?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, and public cloud integration guidance.

faq.question: Does it create deployment scripts?
faq.answer: It can outline automation and IaC approaches, but it does not run provider commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map architecture choices to controls, but final compliance requires organizational evidence.

faq.question: Is it useful for disaster recovery planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers RTO, RPO, backup placement, failover, recovery testing, and business continuity planning.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide workloads, current platforms, compliance needs, latency targets, budget constraints, and migration timeline.
